> Reference for fw, Aphrody and ay, generated from the code

# fw, Aphrody and ay: install and reference

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/

### Start in three commands

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fw.aphrody.com/install.sh | sh
fw --version
fw onboard
```

On Windows, use PowerShell. The [install page](/start/install/) has both.

### What these docs cover

| Section | What you find | Pages |
|---|---|---|
| [Get started](/start/) | Install fw and run it, one action per step | 2 |
| [CLI reference](/cli/) | Every `fw` command, read from `fw --help` | 65 |
| [MCP tools](/mcp/) | Every tool of the fw MCP server with its input schema | 18 |
| [API reference](/api/) | HTTP endpoints of `fw serve`, the edge Worker and ay | 5 |
| [Crates](/crates/) | Workspace crates from `cargo metadata` | 148 |
| [Products](/products/fw/) | fw, Aphrody and ay | 3 |
| [Releases](/releases/) | Installers per platform and the live version | 1 |

### For agents

Every page has a plain markdown copy: add `index.md` to the page address. [llms.txt](/llms.txt) lists all pages and [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) holds them in one file. The [agents guide](/guides/agents/) shows how to connect an agent.

# Get started with fw

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/start/

Each step is one action. Do them in order.

### 1. Open a terminal

On Windows, open PowerShell. On Linux, open any terminal.

### 2. Install fw

Follow the [install page](/start/install/) for your system. It takes one command.

### 3. Check the version

Run this command.

```bash
fw --version
```

The output starts with `fw 2026.11.0` or a newer number.

### 4. Check your machine

```bash
fw doctor
```

The command checks the toolchain, `FX_HOME`, git, API keys and Ollama on port 11434. Fix what it reports, then run it again.

### 5. Go to your project

```bash
cd path/to/your/project
```

### 6. Describe the project to agents

```bash
fw onboard
```

The usage is `fw onboard [dir] | fw onboard export <all|mcp|opencode|zed> [--dir <dir>]`. The command describes the workspace for agents.

### 7. Write the agent config files

```bash
fw onboard export all
```

This writes `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` and `.zed/settings.json` in the project. Open one and check that it lists the fw MCP server.

### 8. Ask the agent a question

```bash
fw ask "what does this project do?"
```

The agent needs a model endpoint. Run `fw models` to see the configured providers.

### 9. Start the server

```bash
fw serve 127.0.0.1:8787
```

The usage is `fw serve [host:port]`. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8787/` in your browser to see the chat page. The server also answers on `/mcp`, `/acp` and `/a2a`: see the [API reference](/api/fw-serve/).

### Next

- [CLI reference](/cli/): every command.
- [Agents guide](/guides/agents/): connect Claude Code, Zed or OpenCode.
- [Learning guide](/guides/learning/): let fw learn from your repository.


---

# Install fw on Linux, macOS and Windows

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/start/install/

Install the `fw` binary. It is one file. The latest `dev` build is `2026.11.21-fc4f4fa`, published 2026-11-21.

#### Linux and macOS

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fw.aphrody.com/install.sh | sh
```

#### Windows

```powershell
irm https://fw.aphrody.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

Check the install:

```bash
fw --version
```

### Update and remove

```bash
fw self-update --check
fw self-update
fw self-uninstall --purge-data
```

`fw self-update` verifies the SHA-256 of the download and keeps the previous binary as `.prev`. `--purge-data` also removes `~/.fx`.

### Release files

The installer picks the file for your system from this list. 3 of 4 files are published. Not published: `fw-aarch64-macos`.

| File | System | Architecture | ABI | Kind | Published |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fw-x86_64-linux-musl` | Linux | x86_64 | musl | binary | yes |
| `fw-x86_64-windows.exe` | Windows | x86_64 | msvc | binary | yes |
| `fw-aarch64-macos` | macOS | aarch64 |  | binary | no |
| `fw_wasm.wasm` | Browser (WebAssembly) | wasm32 |  | wasm | yes |


The table comes from `release.toml`. The [releases page](/releases/) shows the live versions.

| [Learning guide: fw learn and the corpus](/guides/learning/) | Harvest git history, the code graph and docs into a local store and search it with fw learn. Usage lines are read from fw --help. |
| [How this site is generated](/guides/docs-site/) | The docs are generated by fw site from fw --help, the MCP server, cargo metadata, product files and the release manifest, and checked for drift in CI. |

# Agents guide: AGENTS.md, MCP, skills

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/guides/agents/

An agent works best when it can read the rules of a project and call its tools. fw gives it three things: instruction files, an MCP server and skills.

### Instruction files

Put an `AGENTS.md` at the root of the repository. It holds the rules an agent must follow: how to build, how to test, what not to touch. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`; keep it as a short pointer to `AGENTS.md`.

Run `fw onboard [dir] | fw onboard export <all|mcp|opencode|zed> [--dir <dir>]`. It describes the workspace for agents and can export configs for MCP, OpenCode and Zed.

```bash
fw onboard export all
```

### Plain-text docs

This site serves text for machines:

- [llms.txt](/llms.txt) lists every page with a one-line note.
- [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) holds every page in one file.
- Add `index.md` to any page address for the markdown source, for example `/cli/index.md`.

### MCP

`fw mcp | fw mcp <list|add|remove>` serves fw tools over stdio, and `fw serve` serves them over HTTP on `/mcp`. The server lists 17 tools. Each has a page with its input schema: see the [MCP tools](/mcp/).

### Skills

Skills are folders with a `SKILL.md`. The command is `fw skills <list|read|install>`.

```bash
fw skills list
fw skills read <name>
```

### Check your setup

1. Run `fw onboard export mcp` in your project.
2. Open the `.mcp.json` it wrote.
3. Start your agent and ask it to call `fw_status`.


---

# Learning guide: fw learn and the corpus

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/guides/learning/

fw learns locally. It reads your git history, a code graph and your docs, stores them in SQLite, and searches them without a network call.

### Commands

| Command | Usage |
|---|---|
| `fw learn` | fw learn <status\|harvest\|distill\|search\|loop\|systemd> [--xfs-root <dir>] |
| `fw corpus` | fw corpus <sources\|status\|sync\|search\|read\|systemd> [--root <dir>] |
| `fw mem` | fw mem <add\|search\|timeline\|get\|list\|stats\|prune> |
| `fw graph` | fw graph <build <dir> [--json f] [--report f]\|query <question>\|explain <node>\|path <a> <b>\|report\|export> |
| `fw docs` | fw docs <resolve\|query\|ingest\|list> [lib] [topic] [--tokens 4000] |

The table is read from `fw <command> --help`.

### Learn from a repository

1. Go to the repository.
2. Harvest history, graph and docs.

```bash
fw learn harvest
```

3. Look at what was stored.

```bash
fw learn status
```

4. Search it.

```bash
fw learn search "how are releases published"
```

### Run it on a server

`fw learn systemd` prints a systemd unit for a VPS. `fw learn loop` repeats harvest and distill.

### Reference docs

`fw corpus` keeps a polite, resumable copy of design, Android, Chromium, Rust and Cargo docs. `fw learn search` includes it. See the [`fw corpus`](/cli/corpus/) and [`fw learn`](/cli/learn/) pages.


---

# How this site is generated

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/guides/docs-site/

This site is generated. A person edits code, not pages.

### Commands

```bash
fw site gen      # write apps/docs from the code
fw site check    # fail when a generated file differs from the code
fw site llms     # write llms.txt and llms-full.txt
```

### Sources

| Pages | Source |
|---|---|
| [CLI reference](/cli/) | `fw --help` and `fw <command> --help` of the built binary (64 commands) |
| [MCP tools](/mcp/) | `tools/list` of the MCP server in `src/fw_cli.ts` (17 tools) |
| [API reference](/api/) | `fw openapi`, `crates/fw-edge/data` and `ay/docs/auto/openapi.json` |
| [Crates](/crates/) | `cargo metadata --no-deps` (384 packages) |
| [Products](/products/fw/) | `product.toml`, `aphrody/product.toml` and `ay/ay.toml` |
| [Releases](/releases/) | `release.toml` and the live release manifest |
| Colors | `fw-m3 css` from the `[brand]` seed in `product.toml` |

Every page has a `generated` front-matter field with its inputs and a short hash. `fw site check` regenerates in memory and compares. A scheduled workflow refreshes the live site every six hours.

# Products

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/products/

The stack has an order. A product may depend on the ones before it, never on the ones after it.

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [fw: toolchain and agent runtime](/products/fw/) | fw is a Rust toolchain and agent runtime: one binary with a coding agent, MCP, ACP and A2A servers, and local learning. Version 2026.11.21-fc4f4fa. |
| [Aphrody: OS and desktop](/products/aphrody/) | Local-first OS and desktop: GPUI desktop shell, compositor, installer and the Aphrody Studio editor, 100% compatible with the Zed ecosystem. Reference of the… |
| [ay: SDK, cloud and edge](/products/ay/) | ay is the SDK of the Aphrody stack: C ABI, corelib, OpenAPI, design tokens, cloud and edge services. Repository list and release files. |

# fw: toolchain and agent runtime

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/products/fw/

`fw` is the toolchain and agent runtime of the Aphrody stack, number 1 of 5. It is one binary with a coding agent, a Hugging Face client, MCP, ACP and A2A servers, a package manager and local learning.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `fw` |
| Product version | `2026.11.0` |
| Latest release | `2026.11.21-fc4f4fa` |
| Binary | `fw` |
| License | MIT |
| Repository | [aphrody-labs/fw](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/fw) |
| Brand seed | `#e2dbad` |

### Interfaces

- [CLI reference](/cli/): 64 commands.
- [MCP tools](/mcp/): 17 tools.
- [API reference](/api/fw-serve/): `fw serve` endpoints.
- [Crates](/crates/list-fw/): 44 workspace crates.

### Install

See [install fw](/start/install/).

### Release files

| File | System | Architecture | ABI | Kind | Published |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fw-x86_64-linux-musl` | Linux | x86_64 | musl | binary | yes |
| `fw-x86_64-windows.exe` | Windows | x86_64 | msvc | binary | yes |
| `fw-aarch64-macos` | macOS | aarch64 |  | binary | no |
| `fw_wasm.wasm` | Browser (WebAssembly) | wasm32 |  | wasm | yes |

Source: `release.toml`.

# Aphrody: OS and desktop

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/products/aphrody/

Local-first OS and desktop: GPUI desktop shell, compositor, installer and the Aphrody Studio editor, 100% compatible with the Zed ecosystem.

Aphrody is the operating system and desktop of the stack, number 2 of 5. It is a fork of Zed built on GPUI.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Aphrody |
| Tagline | OS and desktop (Zed fork, GPUI) |
| Company | Aphrody Labs |
| URL scheme | `aphrody://` |
| Repository | [aphrody-labs/aphrody](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody) |

|---|---|

| homepage | `https://aphrody.com` |
| releases | `https://releases.aphrody.com` |
| repository | `https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody` |
| server | `https://zed.dev` |
| status | `https://status.aphrody.com` |
| store | `https://aphrody.com/store` |

### Crates

# fw command reference

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/cli/

`fw` is one binary. `fw --help` lists the commands and `fw <command> --help` shows the usage of one. This section has a page for each of the 64 commands, read from those outputs (fw 2026.11.0).

### Global options

These options work with every command.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-C, --directory <DIR>` | Change working directory before running [env: FW_WORKING_DIR] |
| `--config <FILE>` | Path to config file [env: FW_CONFIG] |
| `--offline` | Disable network access [env: FW_OFFLINE] |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON output |
| `--color <WHEN>` | Color output: auto, always, never |
| `-q, --quiet` | Reduce output verbosity |
| `-v, --verbose` | Increase output verbosity |
| `-c` | Resume latest interactive session (when no command given) |
| `-h, --help` | Print help (or `fw <command> --help`) |
| `-V, --version` | Print version and exit |

### Agent & Interactive

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw ask`](/cli/ask/) | `chat` | Run the multi-turn coding agent with tool calls (--model --url --resume --full-access --json) |
| [`fw tool`](/cli/tool/) | `x` | Execute a workspace tool directly (read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob_files, grep_files, shell) |
| [`fw tui`](/cli/tui/) | `m3-tui`, `god` | Launch interactive Material 3 TUI |
| [`fw serve`](/cli/serve/) | `s` | Serve the chat web UI plus /v1/chat/completions, /mcp, /acp, /a2a and /webgpu |

### Files & Media

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw convert`](/cli/convert/) | `cv` | Convert a file into other files: video to SVG frames, Markdown, HTML, JSX and GPUI source (runs fw-video) |
| [`fw google`](/cli/google/) |  | Google Workspace and YouTube: Drive list/export, Sheets get/update, Gmail list/draft (never sends), Calendar events, Docs text, YouTube channels/videos/playlists and video update behind --apply (runs fw-google) |
| [`fw files`](/cli/files/) | `fl` | File manager engine from yazi: sorted listings, MIME and previewer rules, previews, copy/move/remove with progress events, sftp:// paths; JSON lines (runs fw-files) |

### ML, Inference & Heretic

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw infer`](/cli/infer/) | `run` | Send a prompt to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; with --gguf, read the GGUF header and run a Q8_0 dot-product sample (no token generation) |
| [`fw train`](/cli/train/) | `finetune`, `lora` | LoRA SGD demo on a synthetic 32-dim layer; a dataset.jsonl is validated and counted, not trained on; writes an fw-lora-v1 JSON |
| [`fw hf`](/cli/hf/) | `huggingface` | Hugging Face Hub client: search, info, files, pull, safetensors header and tokenizer.json inspection |
| [`fw abliterate`](/cli/abliterate/) | `abl` | Abliteration: `plan` sizes a 7-step pipeline; biprojected, ara, sweep and moe run reference math on synthetic vectors, not model weights |
| [`fw vram`](/cli/vram/) |  | Estimate llama.cpp VRAM, SWA KV cache and the -ngl layer split |
| [`fw heretic`](/cli/heretic/) |  | Heretic TOML preset inspector; `abliterate` runs directional orthogonalization on synthetic vectors |
| [`fw align`](/cli/align/) | `dpo`, `orpo` | DPO, ORPO and KTO loss demo on one synthetic preference pair; no model is aligned |

### Workspace & Protocols

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw repomap`](/cli/repomap/) |  | Repository symbol map (Rust, TS/JS, Python, Go, Kotlin) |
| [`fw watch`](/cli/watch/) |  | Manage persistent scheduled agent watchers (~/.fx/watchers.json) |
| [`fw tune`](/cli/tune/) | `cachy` | CachyOS hardware, sysctl, scx_lavd and ananicy-cpp profiles; x86-64-v3 and mimalloc microbenchmarks |
| [`fw sec`](/cli/sec/) | `deepsec` | Pattern-based scan for secrets and risky code |
| [`fw cluster`](/cli/cluster/) |  | Inference router (KV-cache affinity, prefill/decode split) over the sample topology, or a Kubernetes cluster through kube-rs (runs fw-k8s) |
| [`fw depot`](/cli/depot/) | `gclient` | depot_tools in Rust for Chromium and AOSP: gclient sync/revinfo/getdep/setdep, CIPD, fetch, autoninja, git cl and Gerrit, presubmit, repo manifests, lunch (runs fw-depot) |
| [`fw kernel`](/cli/kernel/) | `linux` | The Linux kernel as pinned files: kernel.toml pins (mainline, stable, CachyOS) against kernel.org releases, shallow sparse submodule sync, UAPI types for bun:ffi, tree-sitter code graph (runs fw-linux) |
| [`fw graph`](/cli/graph/) | `graphify` | Code graph of a tree (tree-sitter Rust, oxc TS/JS, Markdown): calls, imports, communities, god nodes; runs fw-graph |
| [`fw mem`](/cli/mem/) | `memory`, `claude-mem` | Memory store: add, then search (BM25), timeline and get; monthly JSONL shards |
| [`fw docs`](/cli/docs/) | `c7`, `context7` | Resolve and query library docs from crates.io, npm, PyPI, GitHub and llms.txt, cached locally |
| [`fw corpus`](/cli/corpus/) |  | Polite incremental corpus of Google design, Android, Chromium, GitHub, Kotlin, Rust and Cargo docs in per-source SQLite FTS5 stores; `fw learn search` includes it |
| [`fw site`](/cli/site/) |  | Docs site: write the MDX pages of apps/docs from code (fw --help, MCP tools, crates, products, releases), check them for drift, write llms.txt (runs fw-site) |
| [`fw learn`](/cli/learn/) | `autolearn` | Harvest git history, the code graph and docs into a local corpus; search all three; `systemd` prints a unit for a VPS |
| [`fw skills`](/cli/skills/) |  | List, read and install SKILL.md skills |
| [`fw onboard`](/cli/onboard/) | `init-agent` | Describe the workspace for agents and export MCP, OpenCode and Zed configs |
| [`fw workflow`](/cli/workflow/) | `wf` | Run a built-in workflow (discover, abliterate-e2e, pkg-audit, perf-check) |
| [`fw self-install`](/cli/self-install/) |  | Install fw binary into ~/.local/bin with SHA-256 verification |
| [`fw self-update`](/cli/self-update/) | `update`, `upgrade` | Update from GitHub Releases, verify SHA-256, keep the previous binary as .prev |
| [`fw self-uninstall`](/cli/self-uninstall/) |  | Remove the fw binary (--purge-data also removes ~/.fx) |
| [`fw config`](/cli/config/) |  | Read or update ~/.fx/config.json |
| [`fw mcp`](/cli/mcp/) |  | Serve fw's tools as an MCP server over stdio, or manage client MCP servers in ~/.fx/mcp.json |
| [`fw acp`](/cli/acp/) |  | Run Agent Client Protocol JSON-RPC 2.0 server over stdio |
| [`fw sessions`](/cli/sessions/) | `session` | List, inspect, or delete saved agent sessions |
| [`fw permissions`](/cli/permissions/) |  | View or set agent permission mode |
| [`fw models`](/cli/models/) | `provider` | List configured LLM providers & endpoints |
| [`fw workspace`](/cli/workspace/) |  | Show git state and the file index |
| [`fw pr`](/cli/pr/) | `issue` | Read-only git status and diff snapshot |
| [`fw doctor`](/cli/doctor/) |  | Check the toolchain, FX_HOME, git, API keys and Ollama on :11434 |
| [`fw completion`](/cli/completion/) |  | Generate shell completion script |
| [`fw bench`](/cli/bench/) |  | Run local compute, exec or HTTP benchmarks; `perf run` is the monorepo build, size, startup, link, wasm, Workers and GPU harness |
| [`fw help`](/cli/help/) |  | Show help for fw or one command |

### GNU/Linux & Wasm Userland

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw sh`](/cli/sh/) |  | In-process pipeline shell over 40 built-in applets, no child processes |
| [`fw jq`](/cli/jq/) |  | JSON query filter (.a.b[0], keys, length) |
| [`fw tokei`](/cli/tokei/) |  | Lines-of-code counter by language |
| [`fw du`](/cli/du/) |  | Disk usage by directory |
| [`fw bat`](/cli/bat/) |  | Line-numbered file viewer |

### Packages & Dependencies

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`fw init`](/cli/init/) |  | Initialize a project manifest |
| [`fw install`](/cli/install/) | `i` | Install project dependencies |
| [`fw add`](/cli/add/) | `a` | Add a dependency to the project |
| [`fw remove`](/cli/remove/) | `rm`, `uninstall` | Remove a dependency from the project |
| [`fw lock`](/cli/lock/) |  | Generate deterministic fw-pm.lock.json (Cargo + npm + APM) |
| [`fw verify`](/cli/verify/) |  | Verify fw-pm.lock.json against workspace manifests |
| [`fw crates`](/cli/crates/) | `crate` | Crate intelligence over crates.io: ranked search, per-crate score, side-by-side comparison, per-category awesome lists, load-tested framework benchmarks, a stack and project-skeleton generator, and the daily dump sync (runs fw-crates) |
| [`fw info`](/cli/info/) | `resolve` | Fetch crates.io sparse index or npm registry metadata |
| [`fw fetch`](/cli/fetch/) | `download` | Download a .crate or npm .tgz into ~/.fw/cache and verify its SHA-256 |
| [`fw tree`](/cli/tree/) | `scan` | Inspect workspace dependency graph (Cargo + npm + APM) |
| [`fw export`](/cli/export/) | `sbom` | Export CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM |
| [`fw audit`](/cli/audit/) |  | Audit installed dependencies |
| [`fw compile`](/cli/compile/) |  | Compile APM instructions & targets |
| [`fw semver`](/cli/semver/) |  | Evaluate Bun-compatible semver range |


---

# fw site

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/cli/site/

Docs site: write the MDX pages of apps/docs from code (fw --help, MCP tools, crates, products, releases), check them for drift, write llms.txt (runs fw-site)

### Usage

```bash
fw site <gen|check|llms> [--root <dir>] [--fw <binary>]
```

### Subcommands

```bash
fw site gen
fw site check
fw site llms
```

The names come from the usage line.

### Flags

| Flag | Argument |
|---|---|
| `--root` | `<dir>` |
| `--fw` | `<binary>` |
| `--help` |  |

Every command also accepts `-C`, `--directory`, `--offline`, `--json`, `-q` and `-v`. See the [overview](/cli/).

# fw crates

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/cli/crates/

Crate intelligence over crates.io: ranked search, per-crate score, side-by-side comparison, per-category awesome lists, load-tested framework benchmarks, a stack and project-skeleton generator, and the daily dump sync (runs fw-crates)

### Usage

```bash
fw crates <search|info|compare|rank|awesome|bench|stack|sync> [args] [--json|--mdx]
```

### Aliases

`fw crate` runs `fw crates`.

### Subcommands

```bash
fw crates search
fw crates info
fw crates compare
fw crates rank
fw crates awesome
fw crates bench
fw crates stack
fw crates sync
```

The names come from the usage line.

### Global options

Every command also accepts `-C`, `--directory`, `--offline`, `--json`, `-q` and `-v`. See the [overview](/cli/).

### Same group: Packages & Dependencies

[`fw init`](/cli/init/), [`fw install`](/cli/install/), [`fw add`](/cli/add/), [`fw remove`](/cli/remove/), [`fw lock`](/cli/lock/), [`fw verify`](/cli/verify/), [`fw info`](/cli/info/), [`fw fetch`](/cli/fetch/)

### Source

Read from `fw crates --help` of fw 2026.11.0.


---

# fw info

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/cli/info/

Fetch crates.io sparse index or npm registry metadata

### Usage

```bash
fw info <cargo|npm> <pkg>
```

### Aliases

`fw resolve` runs `fw info`.

### Subcommands

```bash
fw info cargo
fw info npm
```

The names come from the usage line.

### Global options

Every command also accepts `-C`, `--directory`, `--offline`, `--json`, `-q` and `-v`. See the [overview](/cli/).

# fw fetch

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/cli/fetch/

Download a .crate or npm .tgz into ~/.fw/cache and verify its SHA-256

### Usage

```bash
fw fetch <cargo|npm> <pkg>
```

### Aliases

`fw download` runs `fw fetch`.

### Subcommands

```bash
fw fetch cargo
fw fetch npm
```

The names come from the usage line.

### Global options

Every command also accepts `-C`, `--directory`, `--offline`, `--json`, `-q` and `-v`. See the [overview](/cli/).

### Same group: Packages & Dependencies

[`fw init`](/cli/init/), [`fw install`](/cli/install/), [`fw add`](/cli/add/), [`fw remove`](/cli/remove/), [`fw lock`](/cli/lock/), [`fw verify`](/cli/verify/), [`fw crates`](/cli/crates/), [`fw info`](/cli/info/)

# fw MCP tools

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/

The fw MCP server exposes 17 tools over JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio. Start it from a fw checkout with `bun src/fw_cli.ts mcp`, or use `fw serve` and post to `/mcp`.

### Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`crates_awesome`](/mcp/crates-awesome/) | The ranked best crates of a crates.io category, or the index of every awesome list when no category is given. |
| [`crates_compare`](/mcp/crates-compare/) | Compare two or more crates side by side with the best crate per metric. |
| [`crates_info`](/mcp/crates-info/) | One crate: score with its components, downloads, dependents, releases, MSRV, licence, advisories, rank overall and per category; live=true adds the live sparse-index record. |
| [`crates_search`](/mcp/crates-search/) | Search the ranked crates.io dataset by words (name, keywords, categories, description); results ordered by relevance then score. |
| [`crates_stack`](/mcp/crates-stack/) | Pick crates from the ranking for a goal in words (for example `web API with Postgres and auth`) and return the choices with reasons and a Cargo project skeleton. |
| [`fw_ai`](/mcp/fw-ai/) | Query Fw AI Brain (FTS5), Soul constitution, Router providers, or Low-Level LTO/AOT matrix. |
| [`fw_ast_parse`](/mcp/fw-ast-parse/) | Parse a source file using Fw's Fat-LTO Rust Tree-sitter C ABI across 12 grammars (rust, typescript, tsx, javascript, python, c, cpp, java, kotlin, go, json, bash). |
| [`fw_bridge`](/mcp/fw-bridge/) | Inspect or dispatch to Fw's absorbed first/third-party subsystems (heretic, neon/REA, craft-libs, craft-anything, ghidra). |
| [`fw_disasm`](/mcp/fw-disasm/) | Disassemble PE entry-point x86-64 instructions using craft-pe + iced-x86 Fat-LTO ABI, or identify any file via craft-sniff. |
| [`fw_learn`](/mcp/fw-learn/) | Run `fw learn` (status, harvest, distill, search, loop). |
| [`fw_pe_inspect`](/mcp/fw-pe-inspect/) | Inspect a Windows PE/COFF binary using craft-pe compiled into Fw's Fat-LTO ABI. |
| [`fw_status`](/mcp/fw-status/) | Return Fw monorepo status, Rust C ABI (v4) health, absorbed modules and plugin status. |
| [`fw_target_scan`](/mcp/fw-target-scan/) | Scan all registered in-repo Fw modules (heretic, neon, craft-libs, craft-anything, native/*, src, tests), run AST probes, and update target/manifest.json. |
| [`fw_tui_terminal`](/mcp/fw-tui-terminal/) | Inspect and run Fw-optimized Microsoft Intelligent Terminal (WTA) and tui-test source-only workflows. |
| [`fw_vfs`](/mcp/fw-vfs/) | Interact with Fw SQLite CAS VFS OS (mounts, ls, read, write). |
| [`kernel_graph`](/mcp/kernel-graph/) | Query the tree-sitter code graph of a pinned Linux kernel tree (symbols, definitions, references, includes, call edges, Kconfig and Kbuild links) with file:line answers. Build it first with `fw kernel graph build` on a host that has the tree. |
| [`kernel_status`](/mcp/kernel-status/) | Linux kernel pins (mainline, stable, CachyOS and its PKGBUILDs from kernel.toml) against kernel.org releases.json (mainline, stable, longterm, linux-next) and the newest CachyOS tags: behind and inconsistent pins, gitlinks, remote tags. |

### Call a tool

Send `initialize`, then `tools/list`, then `tools/call` with the tool name and its arguments. Each tool page has a ready example.

### How this list is made

`fw site` starts the server, sends `tools/list` and reads the answer. A tool added to `src/mcp_server.ts` appears here on the next run.


---

# crates_awesome MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/crates-awesome/

The ranked best crates of a crates.io category, or the index of every awesome list when no category is given.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "crates_awesome",
    "arguments": {}
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | `string` | no |  |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer"
    }
  }
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).


---

# crates_compare MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/crates-compare/

Compare two or more crates side by side with the best crate per metric.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "crates_compare",
    "arguments": {
      "names": []
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | `array` | yes |  |
| `live` | `boolean` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "names": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "live": {
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "names"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).


---

```json
      "name": "<name>"
    }
  }
}
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

```json
  "type": "object",

    "name": {
      "type": "string"
```

# crates_search MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/crates-search/

Search the ranked crates.io dataset by words (name, keywords, categories, description); results ordered by relevance then score.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "crates_search",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "<query>"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `string` | yes |  |
| `category` | `string` | no | crates.io category slug or unique part of it |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "crates.io category slug or unique part of it"
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "query"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).

# fw_ai MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/fw-ai/

Query Fw AI Brain (FTS5), Soul constitution, Router providers, or Low-Level LTO/AOT matrix.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "fw_ai",
    "arguments": {
      "action": "brain_index"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `string: brain_index, brain_search, soul, router, lowlevel_matrix, dedupe` | yes |  |
| `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `model` | `string` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "brain_index",
        "brain_search",
        "soul",
        "router",
        "lowlevel_matrix",
        "dedupe"
      ]
    },
    "query": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "model": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).

# fw_ast_parse MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/fw-ast-parse/

Parse a source file using Fw's Fat-LTO Rust Tree-sitter C ABI across 12 grammars (rust, typescript, tsx, javascript, python, c, cpp, java, kotlin, go, json, bash).

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "fw_ast_parse",
    "arguments": {
      "lang": "<lang>",
      "file": "<file>"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lang` | `string` | yes | Grammar name (rust, typescript, tsx, python, c, cpp, java, json, bash). |
| `file` | `string` | yes | Relative or absolute path to source file. |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "lang": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Grammar name (rust, typescript, tsx, python, c, cpp, java, json, bash)."
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relative or absolute path to source file."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "lang",
    "file"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).


---

```json
  "method": "tools/call",

      "subsystem": "heretic"
    }
  }
}
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subsystem` | `string: heretic, neon, craft, ghidra` | yes | Subsystem name. |

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "subsystem": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "heretic",
        "neon",
        "craft",
        "ghidra"
      ],
      "description": "Subsystem name."
    }
```

# fw_disasm MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/fw-disasm/

Disassemble PE entry-point x86-64 instructions using craft-pe + iced-x86 Fat-LTO ABI, or identify any file via craft-sniff.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "fw_disasm",
    "arguments": {
      "path": "<path>"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `string: disasm, identify` | no | Operation mode. |
| `path` | `string` | yes | Binary or file path. |
| `maxInsns` | `integer` | no | Instruction limit. |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "disasm",
        "identify"
      ],
      "description": "Operation mode."
    },
    "path": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Binary or file path."
    },
    "maxInsns": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 128,
      "description": "Instruction limit."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).


---

# fw_tui_terminal MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/fw-tui-terminal/

Inspect and run Fw-optimized Microsoft Intelligent Terminal (WTA) and tui-test source-only workflows.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "fw_tui_terminal",
    "arguments": {
      "action": "status"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `string: status, wta_config, verify_self` | yes |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "status",
        "wta_config",
        "verify_self"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).

# fw_vfs MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/fw-vfs/

Interact with Fw SQLite CAS VFS OS (mounts, ls, read, write).

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "fw_vfs",
    "arguments": {
      "action": "mounts"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `string: mounts, ls, read, write` | yes |  |
| `path` | `string` | no |  |
| `content` | `string` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "mounts",
        "ls",
        "read",
        "write"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "content": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ]
}
```

# kernel_graph MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/kernel-graph/

Query the tree-sitter code graph of a pinned Linux kernel tree (symbols, definitions, references, includes, call edges, Kconfig and Kbuild links) with file:line answers. Build it first with `fw kernel graph build` on a host that has the tree.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "kernel_graph",
    "arguments": {
      "query": "stats"
    }
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `string: stats, def, refs, callers, callees, includes, included-by, file, config, search, path` | yes |  |
| `operands` | `array` | no | Symbol, file path or CONFIG_ name (two symbols for `path`). |
| `tree` | `string` | no | Pinned tree id: stable (default), mainline, cachyos. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "stats",
        "def",
        "refs",
        "callers",
        "callees",
        "includes",
        "included-by",
        "file",
        "config",
        "search",
        "path"
      ]
    },
    "operands": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "Symbol, file path or CONFIG_ name (two symbols for `path`)."
    },
    "tree": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Pinned tree id: stable (default), mainline, cachyos."
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "query"
  ]
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).


---

# kernel_status MCP tool

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/mcp/kernel-status/

Linux kernel pins (mainline, stable, CachyOS and its PKGBUILDs from kernel.toml) against kernel.org releases.json (mainline, stable, longterm, linux-next) and the newest CachyOS tags: behind and inconsistent pins, gitlinks, remote tags.

### Call it

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "kernel_status",
    "arguments": {}
  }
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offline` | `boolean` | no | Skip the network: only kernel.toml and the git index. |

### Input schema

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "offline": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Skip the network: only kernel.toml and the git index."
    }
  }
}
```

### Server

Part of the fw MCP server. See the [tool list](/mcp/) and the [agents guide](/guides/agents/).

# fw serve API

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/api/fw-serve/

fw control plane

Start the server with `fw serve [host:port]`. The chat page is served on `/`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/a2a` | Agent-to-Agent JSON-RPC 2.0 |
| `POST` | `/acp` | Agent Client Protocol JSON-RPC 2.0 |
| `GET` | `/claw/ranking` | Rust CLI and protocol rankings from fw-hermes-claw |
| `POST` | `/claw/run` | Execute Hermes/OpenClaw grounded goal loop |
| `GET` | `/claw/status` | Hermes/OpenClaw full-Rust runtime status |
| `GET` | `/cluster` | Cluster topology and registered browser WebGPU peers |
| `POST` | `/cluster/peers` | Register a browser WebGPU compute peer (peerId, vramGb, cpuCores) |
| `POST` | `/cluster/route` | KV-cache radix + disaggregated P/D routing decision |
| `POST` | `/graphql` | GraphQL query endpoint |
| `GET` | `/hardware` | OS UAPI/Win32/POSIX/Darwin & GPU/CPU/TPU hardware profile |
| `GET` | `/health` | Server health |
| `POST` | `/mcp` | Streamable HTTP MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (fw-hermes-claw CliToMcpServer) |
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI-compatible chat completion routed across hybrid cluster |
| `GET` | `/v1/crates/{op}` | Crate intelligence over crates.io: op is search, info, compare, rank, awesome or stack; arguments in the query (query, name, names, category, goal, limit, live) |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | OpenAI-compatible models list |
| `POST` | `/v1beta/decisions` | Gemini Decision 1 calibrated zero-token decisions |
| `GET` | `/webgpu` | Browser page that runs a WebGPU compute shader and reports the result |

### Source

Read from `fw openapi`.

# fw edge Worker API

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/api/fw-edge/

Unified Cloudflare Edge OS Worker: Durable Object SQLite VFS, 3-tier execution (DO POSIX, Dynamic Worker Loader CodeMode, Sandbox microVM), Gatekeeper policy engine, autonomous learning log, and OpenAI / MCP / ACP / A2A protocol gateway.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/.well-known/agent.json` | A2A AgentCard |
| `POST` | `/a2a` | A2A JSON-RPC 2.0 (tasks/send, tasks/get) |
| `POST` | `/acp` | ACP JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, session/new, session/prompt) |
| `GET` | `/api/learn/events` | List autonomous learning log events |
| `POST` | `/api/learn/events` | Append learning event (DO SQLite + K2 + Basin Pipelines) |
| `GET` | `/api/learn/status` | Autonomous learning log metrics and sink readiness |
| `GET` | `/drive/_id/{fileId}` | Drive CDN by file id, limited to the shared root folder |
| `GET` | `/drive/_whoami` | Identity from the Cloudflare Access token (user email or service-token client id) |
| `GET` | `/drive/{path}` | Drive CDN behind Cloudflare Access: folder listing (JSON or HTML) or file bytes from the R2 cache, Range and ETag aware |
| `GET` | `/health` | Edge OS health and active bindings |
| `POST` | `/mcp` | Streamable HTTP MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) |
| `GET` | `/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 schema |
| `GET` | `/os/catalog` | Verified Nov 2026 Cloudflare Edge OS ecosystem catalog |
| `GET` | `/os/gatekeeper` | List Gatekeeper capability rules |
| `POST` | `/os/gatekeeper` | Evaluate or upsert Gatekeeper capability policies |
| `GET` | `/os/tiers` | 3-tier execution architecture and live binding readiness |
| `POST` | `/os/vfs/exec` | 3-tier execution router (Tier-0 DO POSIX, Tier-1 LOADER CodeMode, Tier-2 Sandbox microVM) |
| `GET` | `/os/vfs/ls` | List tenant SQLite VFS entries |
| `POST` | `/os/vfs/ls` | List tenant SQLite VFS entries |
| `GET` | `/os/vfs/read` | Read file from tenant SQLite VFS / R2 spillover |
| `POST` | `/os/vfs/read` | Read file from tenant SQLite VFS / R2 spillover |
| `GET` | `/os/vfs/stat` | Stat tenant SQLite VFS path |
| `POST` | `/os/vfs/stat` | Stat tenant SQLite VFS path |
| `POST` | `/os/vfs/write` | Write file to tenant SQLite VFS with Gatekeeper check |
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | OpenAI-compatible chat (stream or not) via Cloudflare Workers AI; 503 without the AI binding |
| `POST` | `/v1/embeddings` | OpenAI-compatible embeddings with optional Vectorize upsert |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | OpenAI-compatible model list |

### Source

Read from `crates/fw-edge/data/openapi_paths.json`.

# API standards and contract sources

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/api/standards/

### Current standards

The formats the stack follows, with the live version read on the date of the research.

| Layer | Standard | Live version |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP APIs | OpenAPI (OAI/OpenAPI-Specification) | 3.2.1, 2026-09-10 |
| Query APIs | GraphQL (graphql/graphql-spec) | September2026, 2026-11-12 |
| Query APIs | GraphQL over HTTP (graphql/graphql-over-http) | September2026, 2026-11-13 |
| Events and queues | AsyncAPI | v3.1.0, 2026-01-31 |
| Data shapes | JSON Schema 2020-12 (json-schema-org/json-schema-spec, no GitHub release; head 2026-11-19) | 2020-12 |
| RPC | Protocol Buffers | v36.2, 2026-09-17 |
| RPC | Connect: `connectrpc` crate | 0.9.1 |
| RPC | gRPC: `tonic` crate | 0.14.9 |
| Agent tools | MCP | 2026-07-28 |
| Agent to agent | A2A | v1.0.1, 2026-05-28 |
| Service models (AWS-style IDL) | Smithy | 1.75.0, 2026-11-12 |
| Link previews | Open Graph protocol, ogp.me | `og:title`, `og:type`, `og:image` (with `:url`, `:secure_url`, `:type`, `:width`, `:height`, `:alt`), `og:url`, `og:description`, `og:audio`, `og:determiner` |
| Wasm components | Component Model WIT (WebAssembly/component-model, no release; head 2026-11-19) | `wit-bindgen` 0.63.0 |

### What exists today

The contracts present in each repository today.

| Repo | Contracts present |
|---|---|
| fw | `crates/fw-a2a/proto/a2a.proto` and the google.api protos; `crates/fw-edge/data/openapi_{paths,description}.json`; the MCP engine `crates/fw-proto/src/mcp.rs` (152/152 on the suite at 2026-07-28); 17 C headers; `schemars` in fw-proto, fw-toolcall, fw-m3 and fw-a2a |
| aphrody | Zed's collaboration RPC in `crates/proto/proto/*.proto` (11 files); 2 C headers; JSON Schema through `schemars` in settings_content, agent, gpui and others |
| ay | `docs/auto/openapi.json`; the WebAssembly component interface `corelib/wit/ay-corelib.wit` with WASI `io` and `cli` deps; 8 C headers |

Missing everywhere:

- **No single source.** Each product has no one source of truth for its contracts; the OpenAPI files are written by hand or generated in one place.
- **Missing formats:**
  - no GraphQL schema;
  - no AsyncAPI for events and queues;
  - no Open Graph metadata contract for the sites;
  - no generated TypeScript, Kotlin, Python or C# types.
- **Unchecked bindings:** no ABI check on the C headers, and no AST or IR contract.

# Workspace crates

Source: https://docs.aphrody.com/crates/

The Cargo workspace has 384 packages. They come from `cargo metadata --no-deps`.

| Repository | Packages | With a page | List |
|---|---|---|---|

| ay crates | 13 | 13 | [full list](/crates/list-ay/) |
| Aphrody crates | 327 | 86 | [full list](/crates/list-aphrody/) |

A crate gets its own page when it belongs to fw or ay, or when it has a description. The lists show all packages.

Zero-FFmpeg pure-Rust multimedia player, studio, WGSL GPU YUV/HDR/scopes pipeline, HLS/DASH ingest, declarative programmatic video engine (composition format, keyframes, springs, transitions, captions, H.264 MP4 export), and video intelligence index.

### Package

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Part of | Aphrody crates |
| Source | [`aphrody/crates/aphrody_media`](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/fw/tree/main/aphrody/crates/aphrody_media) |
| License | Apache-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later |
| Edition | `2024` |


### Targets

| Kind | Name |
|---|---|
| lib | `aphrody_media` |

### Workspace dependencies

[`brand`](/crates/brand/). It also uses 29 crates from outside the workspace.

### Used by

`aphrody_cli`, [`aphrody_desktop`](/crates/aphrody_desktop/), [`aphrody_video`](/crates/aphrody_video/)

### Features

`audio-native`, `craft-codecs`, `default`, `ingest`, `motion`, `player`, `studio`, `video-encode`, `wasm`, `watch`

### Build

Run this from the repository root.

```bash
cargo build --release -p aphrody_media
```

Process supervision primitives shared by the llama-server supervisor, the command sandbox and the training runner: process groups that die with their owner (Linux session + killpg, Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE), detached daemons, liveness probes, elevated execution without a new console window (Sudo for Windows inline, UAC, sudo-rs), free-port allocation, advisory file locks and the single-GPU lease (shared for inference, exclusive for training).
